advisor_identified: William D. (William Dalton/Bill) Wray, historian of Japanese business and shipping at the University of British Columbia.

doctorate.title: Mitsubishi and the N.Y.K. line, 1870-1894: the beginnings of the modern Japanese shipping industry

evidence.says: UBC History identifies Bill Wray as a researcher in Japanese business and industrial history, especially shipping; its publication list names W.D. Wray as author of Mitsubishi and the N.Y.K., 1870-1914.
Jeffrey W. Alexander, Japan’s Motorcycle Wars (2008), acknowledgments p. xi, describes the project as beginning at UBC and names William Wray as his advisor.
The library authority record identifies William Dalton Wray as a variant of William D. Wray and groups the Harvard thesis with the same books listed on his UBC faculty page.
Catalogues the matching thesis, presented by William Dalton Wray, with the explicit degree note: Thesis (Ph.D.)--Harvard University, 1976. The title and institution match the linked AHA dissertation.

notes: The linked dissertation is his: author, institution and distinctive title match the catalogue and UBC publication trail. CiNii dates the PhD thesis to 1976, whereas the supplied AHA record gives 1977; the reason for this one-year discrepancy and the precise degree-conferral year were not independently established.
